chunks: “Be more hopeful for what you do not expect than for what you expect. Indeed, Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام went out to obtain fire for his family, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke to him, and he returned as a prophet. And the Queen of Saba went out and submitted with Sulayman عليه السلام. And the magicians of Fir'awn went out seeking honor for Fir'awn, but they returned as believers.”

key_terms.نَارًا: fire, which Musa عليه السلام sought for his family
key_terms.يَقْتَبِسُ: seeking to take or bring back a flame of fire

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali عليه السلام teach believers to hope for the unexpected mercy and guidance of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a believer should not restrict hope to expected outcomes, because Allah can bring immense guidance and transformation from situations that seem ordinary or even contrary to one's intention. It illustrates this through the examples of Musa عليه السلام, the Queen of Saba, and the magicians of Fir'awn, all of whom encountered unexpected divine change.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3609 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"Be more hopeful for what you do not expect than for what you expect. Indeed, Moses, son of Imran (as), went out to fetch fire for his family, but Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, spoke to him, and he returned as a prophet. And the Queen of Sheba went out and embraced Islam with Solomon (as). And the magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking honor for Pharaoh but returned as believers."
